IEEE Members Weigh In Select option to display slide Cybersecurity Simulations Cybersecurity Simulations Cybersecurity "Because most connected systems use common off-the-shelf components, everything is now hackable, including medical devices and their networks," says Florence Hudson, chair of the IEEE 2933 Working Group. To address this, the IEEE 2933 standard was developed, outlining the steps users would take to ensure that the medical equipment they develop and interact with is trustworthy in multiple environments. "From discussions with various health care providers over the years, this standard is long overdue," Hudson adds. Read the full article See how IEEE helps raise the world's standards Florence Hudson Chair of the IEEE 2933 Working Group, Founder and CEO, FDHint Executive Director, Northeast Big Data Innovation Hub at Columbia University Simulations IEEE Senior member Sena Kizildemir uses simulations to study how buildings fail under extreme events, such as impacts and explosions. “Simulations help us understand what could happen before it occurs in real life,” she says, “to be able to better plan for it.” Back when the two airplanes hit the World Trade Center on 11 September 2001, skyscrapers had not been designed or constructed with that kind of catastrophic structural failure in mind. “You’re creating something to help people.
